rationale: Interpreted the command-coverage receipt and fixed the harness omission it exposed. The result events show the same zero StoreConfiguration calls for all three dual-interface triggers (voter address change, AddNonvoter, RemoveServer) with 6, 6 and 5 ApplyBatch configuration entries and the control at 6 and 0, so the missing callback is not specific to one command; but the declared comparisons were unresolved because the setup event lacked the trigger field used as identity, so this update cites the result events for those values, records that limitation, and submits a corrected revision that adds the field to the setup event with the same cases and comparisons. No earlier receipt is withdrawn and no claim is weakened: the finding rests on the first two executions' satisfied comparisons plus these event values.

interpretations.rationale: The question was whether an FSM implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore still receives StoreConfiguration for a committed configuration change, as that interface documents, or only through ApplyBatch. The execution answers that it receives only ApplyBatch: in the dual-interface case the recorder shows 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries (parsed result event 3), while the ConfigurationStore-only control shows 6 and 0 (result event 1), with the setup events (0 and 2) matched as admissions and every comparison resolving. The source gives the mechanism: runFSM computes batchingEnabled once, and once it is true every batch goes to applyBatch, which forwards LogCommand and LogConfiguration entries to ApplyBatch and never calls StoreConfiguration; StoreConfiguration is reached only from applySingle, which the batched path does not use. What makes this a defect rather than a naming preference is the purpose the interface states for itself: storing configuration changes so that a persistent FSM state can behave as a complete snapshot and recover without an external one. An application that implements ConfigurationStore for that purpose, and also batches its applies for throughput, gets no callback and no error, so its durable state silently lacks the configuration it was promised. The scope is bounded and I record it plainly: the same entries do reach ApplyBatch, which BatchingFSM documents as receiving LogConfiguration, so an implementation that handles configuration changes in both places loses nothing observable, and the defect is the silent failure of the documented callback rather than lost information. A repeat of the same fixed experiment reproduced both counts exactly (receipt a5809ed4b5024b17adfebf093d3316f5, result events at parsed indices 1 and 3): the dual-interface FSM recorded 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries, the ConfigurationStore-only control recorded 6 and 0, and all four comparisons resolved as before. The account therefore rests on two executions rather than one, and the counts being identical across them is what makes the zero credible rather than an artifact of a single run's timing. A third execution covered other configuration commands and its result events carry the same shape (receipt f5bf67e282cb41c185854215b5b28e34, result events at parsed indices 1, 3, 5 and 7): the dual-interface FSM recorded 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6, 6 and 5 ApplyBatch configuration entries after a voter address change, an AddNonvoter and a RemoveServer respectively, while the ConfigurationStore-only control recorded 6 and 0. Its declared comparisons came back unresolved rather than satisfied because the setup event did not carry the trigger field the identity used, so a corrected revision that adds that field to the setup event is submitted with this update; the values themselves are read from the result events, which carry the trigger and both counters. What the run adds is that the missing callback is not specific to one command: three different configuration changes produced the same zero.

knowledge.assertion: An FSM implementing both interfaces receives configuration changes only through ApplyBatch; two executions of the same probe recorded the same zero and six counts.

counterevidence: The configuration entry is not lost: BatchingFSM documents that ApplyBatch receives LogConfiguration entries, and the receipt shows all 6 deliveries there, so an application handling both paths is unaffected.

The combination is unusual rather than forbidden: nothing in either interface documents mutual exclusion, but an application that implements only one of them sees the documented behaviour, as the control case shows.
The trigger was a single configuration change (moving an existing voter's address); the same code path handles every LogConfiguration entry, but other change commands were not measured.
limitations: The command-coverage revision measured all three triggers with the dual-interface FSM and the control, but its declared comparisons were unresolved because the setup event did not carry the trigger field, so those values are cited from the result events rather than from satisfied comparisons; a corrected revision is submitted with this update.

The interactions are measured in two executions of the same fixed probe, which agree exactly (dual-interface FSM 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries; control 6 and 0), but both use three-voter clusters built by the repository's own helper with a shared recorder.
The consequence for an application's recovery is argued from the interface's stated purpose rather than demonstrated by recovering an FSM that missed the callback.

scope.description: Four cases as in the previous revision - a ConfigurationStore-only control and three dual-interface cases triggered by a voter address change, an AddNonvoter and a RemoveServer - each reporting the StoreConfiguration and ApplyBatch configuration counts, with the setup event now carrying the same trigger identifier as the result event so the admission can be matched.
assumptions: All three commands are legal on a three-voter cluster, as before.
The setup and result events now share batching_fsm and trigger, which is the identity the comparisons use.
The recorder is still shared across the cluster's FSMs.
excluded: DemoteVoter and the deprecated Promote command.

experiment.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with three peers, bootstrapping and the in-memory test configuration, and a MakeFSMFunc returning either an FSM implementing FSM and ConfigurationStore or one that also implements ApplyBatch, all recording into a shared recorder. The case emits assurance_config_store_setup with the batching flag, the trigger name, the leader and target identities and the peer count, issues exactly one configuration command according to the trigger (AddVoter with a new address for the target voter, AddNonvoter for a fresh identity, or RemoveServer of the target follower), waits up to five seconds for a callback counter to become non-zero, waits a further 200ms, and emits assurance_config_store_result with the same trigger and batching flags plus the command's error and the counts. The harness is TestAssuranceConfigurationStoreWithBatching.
